Hi Maya — great questions, and thanks for the VAT doc. Quick summary below (high-level) and I'll pull in finance/partner ops for any items that need DocuSign or formal evidence.

1) AWS Marketplace vs Seller Private Offer
   - If the deal is transacted through AWS Marketplace (AWS collects and invoices the customer), AWS typically acts as the billing intermediary. In that case, Redwood receives settlement from AWS and we do not issue a customer invoice to CloudBridge — AWS will invoice the end customer.
   - For Seller Private Offer (SPO) there are cases where the reseller/partner handles billing; we need to confirm the procurement/{CloudBridge} PO path.

2) GCP / Azure Marketplace nuances
   - GCP and Azure have similar marketplace modes but different tax treatments by region. Often the marketplace is considered the taxable vendor in EU VAT OSS scenarios, which means the marketplace collects VAT at checkout unless an exemption (reverse charge) is documented.

3) EU VAT reverse-charge evidence
   - For reverse charge to apply we generally need: the buyer's valid VAT ID (format-validated), a brief statement of business use, and a copy of VAT registration. For some marketplaces, the marketplace operator will be the deemed supplier and reverse charge won't apply even if buyer has a VAT ID. We can accept CloudBridge's VAT registration but may additionally need the buyer's VAT number and a signed declaration.

4) W-9 / W-8 forms
   - For US-domiciled buyers we request a completed W-9 (tax reporting). For non-US entities we accept W-8BEN-E where appropriate. If the transaction is billed by AWS (marketplace), AWS may handle withholding and US tax reporting.

Hi Maya — looping back with a concise checklist and the documents we'll need to close the billing/tax loop. I've attached the fillable W-9 and our VAT evidence checklist for ease of upload.

Short answers up front:
- If the customer purchases directly from AWS Marketplace (transactable listing), AWS is the billing party to the customer and Redwood receives settlement from AWS. CloudBridge will receive the AWS invoice (not Redwood's).
- If the contract is executed as a reseller/co-sell where CloudBridge is the billing entity, Redwood will issue invoices to CloudBridge and we require standard tax forms and PO evidence.
- For EU reverse-charge: we accept a copy of your VAT registration (we have this) plus the buyer's VAT number and a short commercial use declaration. If the marketplace operator (e.g., AWS/EU) is the deemed supplier, reverse-charge does not apply; in that case VAT is charged at checkout by the marketplace.

Checklist (what we need from CloudBridge to proceed):
1) Completed, signed W-9 (if CloudBridge will be billed as a US entity) OR W-8BEN-E (if billing entity is non-US). Use the attached Redwood_W9_Fillable.pdf or the DocuSign link below.
2) Buyer VAT number(s) for any EU-based end customers where reverse-charge is being claimed.
3) Copy of CloudBridge's VAT registration (we have this) and a one-line statement confirming business use of the purchased software.
4) Purchase Order (PO) with billing entity name exactly as it appears on tax docs.
5) Confirmation of marketplace mode: transactable listing (AWS bills customer) vs reseller (CloudBridge bills customer).

Notes on withholding & special cases:
- If a local tax authority requires withholding on payments to Redwood, we will need official government forms/evidence; that is handled case-by-case and may impact net settlement amounts.
- For multi-entity customers, invoices must be mapped to the specific legal entity; please include the exact billing legal name and tax ID on the PO.

DocuSign links: https://docusign.com/link/example-w9 (W-9)

Attachments included: Redwood_W9_Fillable.pdf, VAT_Evidence_Checklist.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx
